mcqs.question: Consider two cases: (i) a transversal cuts two parallel lines, and (ii) the same transversal cuts two lines that are not parallel. Which statement correctly compares the angle relationships in the two cases?

options.A: In case (i) the transversal creates pairs of equal corresponding angles, while in case (ii) corresponding angles are generally unequal.
options.B: In case (i) the transversal always creates right angles, while in case (ii) it creates obtuse angles.
options.C: In case (ii) alternate interior angles are always equal, unlike case (i).
options.D: The presence of a transversal does not affect any angle relationships in either case.

mcqs.answer: In case (i) the transversal creates pairs of equal corresponding angles, while in case (ii) corresponding angles are generally unequal.
mcqs.explanation: When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, each pair of corresponding angles are equal (e.g., top‑left with top‑right). If the two lines are not parallel, the corresponding angles need not be equal because the interior angles of the intersected lines are different. Options B, C and D describe incorrect or irrelevant statements.

mcqs.question: In the diagram, lines l and m are cut by transversal t. If angle 1 (formed by line l and t) measures 70°, which of the following could be the measure of its corresponding angle on line m?
mcqs.explanation: Corresponding angles are located in the same relative position at each intersection of the transversal with the two lines. Because l and m are parallel, the corresponding angle to the 70° angle must also be 70°. The other measures would violate the corresponding‑angle property.

mcqs.question: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, which pair of angles are alternate interior angles?

options.A: Angles located between the two lines on opposite sides of the transversal.
options.B: Angles on the same side of the transversal and inside the two lines.
options.C: Angles that lie outside the two lines.
options.D: Angles that are vertically opposite each other.

mcqs.answer: Angles located between the two lines on opposite sides of the transversal.
mcqs.explanation: Alternate interior angles are the two angles that lie between the parallel lines but on opposite sides of the transversal. Option B describes interior angles on the same side, option C describes exterior angles, and option D describes vertical angles, none of which are alternate interior angles.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify interior angles on the same side of a transversal
mcqs.question: Identify the pair of interior angles that lie on the same side of a transversal intersecting two parallel lines.

options.A: Angles between the two lines and on the same side of the transversal.
options.B: Angles between the two lines but on opposite sides of the transversal.

mcqs.answer: Angles between the two lines and on the same side of the transversal.
mcqs.explanation: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal are the two angles that are inside the parallel lines and lie on the same side of the transversal; they are supplementary. Option B describes alternate interior angles, while C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the 'corresponding angles' property for parallel lines and distinguishes it from the 'alternate interior angles' property?

options.A: Corresponding angles are in matching corners when a transversal cuts parallel lines; they are equal, whereas alternate interior angles are on opposite sides of the transversal and also equal.
options.B: Corresponding angles are always right angles; alternate interior angles are never equal.
options.C: Corresponding angles are formed only outside the parallel lines, while alternate interior angles are formed only inside.
options.D: Corresponding angles are equal only when the transversal is perpendicular to the parallel lines.

mcqs.answer: Corresponding angles are in matching corners when a transversal cuts parallel lines; they are equal, whereas alternate interior angles are on opposite sides of the transversal and also equal.
mcqs.explanation: The correct definition states that corresponding angles occupy the same relative position at each intersection and are equal when the lines are parallel. Alternate interior angles are a different pair (inside the lines, opposite sides) that are also equal. Options B, C, and D contain false statements.

mcqs.learning_point: Determine whether lines are parallel from angle relationships
mcqs.question: If a transversal cuts two lines and creates a pair of interior angles on the same side that sum to 180°, what can be concluded about the two lines?

options.C: The two lines intersect at a right angle.
options.D: No conclusion can be drawn about their relationship.

mcqs.explanation: When interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary (sum to 180°), the lines intersected by the transversal are parallel. Options B and C refer to right angles, which is unrelated to this criterion, and D is incorrect because the angle relationship gives a definite conclusion.

mcqs.question: In the figure, line AB is crossed by line CD at point E. Which of the following statements correctly describes line CD as a transversal?

options.A: Line CD intersects line AB at a single point, creating several pairs of angles, thus it is a transversal.
options.B: Line CD is parallel to AB, so it cannot be a transversal.
options.C: A transversal must be perpendicular to the line it meets, which CD is not.
options.D: Only lines that intersect two distinct lines can be transversals, and CD meets only one line.

mcqs.answer: Line CD intersects line AB at a single point, creating several pairs of angles, thus it is a transversal.
mcqs.explanation: A transversal is any line that intersects two (or more) other lines. In the given example, CD meets AB, forming angles, satisfying the definition. Options B, C, and D misstate the definition of a transversal.

mcqs.question: A road (transversal) cuts across two railway tracks that are parallel. If the angle between the road and the nearer track is 55°, what is the measure of the corresponding angle formed with the farther track?
mcqs.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when a transversal cuts parallel lines. Therefore the angle made with the farther track must also be 55°. The other options would violate the corresponding‑angle property.
